what_happened: In job yckz, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job moves code between modules. The reading had a criterion that checked callers by relying on the producer's report. The verifier never sees that report, so it could not judge the criterion. The user replaced it with two checks the verifier can run itself. One is a Grep showing that no file outside the moved module's directory names a moved item by its old module path. The other compares the test list before and after the move, using cargo test -- --list output. This is the same correction the user made one job earlier, in vrsk.
cause: The correction from vrsk did not carry over to the next job. The reading stage has no rule that every criterion must name evidence the verifier can see itself, which means the snapshot, commands it runs, and its own tools. It is not told that the producer's report is invisible to the verifier. Nothing checks each criterion's evidence source before the reading is accepted. For module-move jobs, the default way to check callers is to cite the report, so the same flaw recurs. Only the user, who knows what the verifier sees, catches it.
prevention: Add a reading-acceptance check. Every criterion must name an evidence source the verifier can observe: a Grep or command it runs, or a file in the snapshot. A criterion that cites the producer's report, or "the producer confirms", is rejected before the reading is accepted. Also add to the reading brief the standing templates for move and refactor jobs: a Grep for old module paths outside the moved directory, and a before/after cargo test -- --list comparison.
proposed_request: Make Athena reject a reading whose acceptance criteria depend on evidence the verifier cannot see. Outcome: before a reading is accepted, each criterion must name an evidence source the verifier can observe by itself (a snapshot file, a Grep, or a command it can run). Any criterion that rests on the producer's report is refused and the reading is regenerated. For jobs that move code between modules, the reading brief should offer two standard checks. First, a Grep showing no file outside the moved module's directory names a moved item by its old module path. Second, a comparison of cargo test -- --list output before and after the move. Acceptance: a test shows a reading with a report-based criterion is refused. A test shows a reading with Grep and command-based criteria is accepted. The reading brief names the two standard move checks. The reading brief's token budget test still passes.
